title: Bram and the Autopsy
premise: Vesper Eastwick, a reclusive estate lawyer who has spent her career among the dead on paper, is hired by a dying client who pays in advance for a strange service: to prove that his own murder will not happen. When he dies exactly as predicted and the coroner's report is quietly falsified, Vesper realizes the 'autopsy' she must perform is not of a body but of a buried crime — one that requires finding Bram, a witness everyone insists died years ago, before the statute of limitations expires in ninety days. Following a trail of forged death certificates, Vesper discovers that Bram is alive, hidden, and that her own erased past is tangled in the same conspiracy. In the end, Vesper exposes the killers at a probate hearing, chooses to reclaim her real name, and gains the found family she never believed she deserved.
about_author: Silas Sandoval is a former county records clerk who spent eleven years filing death certificates before turning to fiction, giving his mysteries an unsettling documentary precision. He writes from a coastal town in Maine, where he claims every will he's ever read taught him more about the living than the dead.

chapters.title: The Client Who Paid in Advance
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. A gaunt stranger named Aldous Crane hires Vesper to draft a will — and to investigate, after his death, whether he was murdered. He pays triple, in cash, and refuses to name suspects. The beat: unease; Vesper, who prefers paper to people, feels seen through by this man who knows too much about her.

chapters.title: Ninety Days
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Crane reveals a statute of limitations expires in ninety days on an old crime, and that proving his murder would reopen it. He mentions only one name: Bram, 'the witness who is dead.' The beat: reluctant curiosity; Vesper accepts not from compassion but because the case smells like forgery, her specialty.

chapters.title: A Will That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Researching Crane's assets, Vesper finds a prior will filed eleven years ago under a seal she recognizes — the same clerk's stamp used on documents from her own erased hometown. The beat: dread; the case has brushed against the life she buried, and she considers returning the fee.

chapters.title: The Death of Aldous Crane
chapters.summary: Crane's housekeeper Marta's POV. Marta finds Crane dead at the base of his staircase, an apparent fall, just nineteen days into the engagement. She notices his study ransacked and a burned smell in the fireplace. The beat: grief sharpening into suspicion; Marta mails Vesper a key Crane left for her.

chapters.title: Autopsy of Paperwork
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. The official autopsy rules accidental death within hours — suspiciously fast. Vesper obtains the preliminary report and spots an impossible detail: the examiner signed off before the body arrived. The beat: cold fury; the machinery of the state itself has been bent, and Vesper knows exactly how such bending is done.

chapters.title: Marta's Key
chapters.summary: Alternating Vesper/Marta POV. Meeting in a diner, Marta gives Vesper the key and describes Crane's final weeks: phone calls about 'Bram,' a visitor with a county badge. The beat: fragile alliance; two women who trusted no one begin, awkwardly, to trust each other.

chapters.title: What the Fire Left
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. In Crane's locked study, Vesper finds a half-burned photograph: three young people at a lakeside, faces intact except one — circled, labeled 'Bram.' The lake town is hers. The beat: vertigo; the case is no longer about Crane's death but about something Vesper fled from decades ago.

chapters.title: Dead Man Talking
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. County records show Bram Hollis died at seventeen — drowning, same lake, same summer as the fire in Vesper's memory. But the certificate bears the same anomalous clerk's stamp as Crane's fast-tracked autopsy. The beat: grim recognition; someone has been manufacturing deaths for years, and Vesper once lived inside that machine.

chapters.title: The Examiner Who Signed Early
chapters.summary: Deputy coroner Ruth Okafor's POV. Ruth, pressured to sign the Crane report by an anonymous superior, kept a copy of the original findings showing ligature marks. Terrified but principled, she contacts Vesper anonymously. The beat: moral courage; the conspiracy's first crack appears from inside it.

chapters.title: Someone Is Reading My Mail
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Vesper's office is searched, files photocopied, a threat left in the form of a document from her old life — proof her enemies know who she was. The beat: fear curdling into resolve; invisibility, her lifelong armor, has failed, so she decides to fight in the open.

chapters.title: Ruth Comes In From the Cold
chapters.summary: Ruth's POV. Ruth meets Vesper and hands over the true autopsy: Crane was strangled, then staged. She names the pressure's source — a judge connected to the lake town's old land trust. The beat: solidarity; Vesper promises protection, meaning it, surprising herself with how much she means it.

chapters.title: The Land Trust
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Digging into probate archives, Vesper maps the conspiracy: a land trust that absorbed estates of everyone who died near the lake over thirty years, all processed through one sealed docket. The beat: intellectual triumph shadowed by horror; the murders were bookkeeping.

chapters.title: Bram Was a Girl
chapters.summary: Marta's POV. Marta, following a separate thread through Crane's letters, discovers 'Bram' was Abraham's nickname — for Abigail Bramwell, a girl declared drowned whose body was never found. The beat: revelation reframing everything; the witness isn't hiding from the killers, she's hiding from what she saw them do to her family.

chapters.title: Ninety Minus Forty-One
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. With forty-nine days left, Vesper traces Abigail Bramwell to a woman living quietly under another name three states away — and finds the trail watched. A tail follows Vesper home. The beat: escalating menace; the hunters know how close she is, and the clock is audible now.

chapters.title: The Lake in Winter
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Vesper returns to her hometown for the first time in decades, walking the frozen shore where Abigail 'drowned' and where Vesper's own childhood ended. Memories surface: a night, a fire, a girl pulled from the water alive. The beat: painful reckoning; Vesper admits her silence made her complicit in the first cover-up.

chapters.title: Abigail
chapters.summary: Abigail's POV. Abigail, living as 'Nell,' receives Vesper. She saw the trust's founders kill her father and stage her drowning; she has stayed dead for thirty years because staying dead kept her safe. The beat: mutual recognition between two women who erased themselves; Abigail agrees to testify only if Vesper stands beside her as counsel — and as family.

chapters.title: They Burn the Evidence
chapters.summary: Ruth's POV. The conspirators torch the records annex, destroying the sealed docket, and Ruth survives an 'accident' meant for her. She brings Vesper the one thing saved: her private copy of Crane's true autopsy. The beat: darkest hour; the paper trail is ash, and testimony is all that remains.

chapters.title: Ninety Minus Twelve
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. With twelve days left, Vesper builds the case from fragments: the early-signed autopsy, the cloned clerk's stamp, the trust's beneficiary chain, and Crane's letter naming his murderers — the judge and the trust's executor. The beat: quiet ferocity; the lawyer who hid behind procedure now weaponizes it.

chapters.title: The Probate Hearing
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV, courtroom. At the emergency hearing on Crane's contested will, Vesper enters evidence of murder, calls Ruth, then springs the impossible: 'the court will hear from Abigail Bramwell, presumed deceased thirty-one years.' The gallery erupts. The beat: cathartic climax; the dead woman speaks, and the room cannot look away.

chapters.title: What Abigail Saw
chapters.summary: Abigail's POV. Under oath, Abigail testifies to her father's murder, the staged drowning, and the trust's ledger of bought deaths — including, she reveals, the falsified record of Vesper's own identity, which the trust used to erase a witness long ago: Vesper herself. The beat: shattering exposure; Vesper's secret becomes evidence, and liberation.

chapters.title: Statute Expired, Case Opened
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. The judge and executor are indicted; the statute's expiry is mooted because the fraud tolls it anew. Crane's will, validated, leaves everything to Marta and to a fund for witnesses in hiding. The beat: hard-won justice; the law Vesper served finally protects the people it was built to bury.

chapters.title: Bram and the Autopsy
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV, epilogue. Spring: Vesper, Marta, Ruth, and Abigail share a slow dinner above Vesper's new office, its sign reading 'Eastwick & Bramwell.' Vesper signs a document with her true name for the first time in decades. The beat: warm resolution; the autopsy is complete — not of a body, but of a buried life, exhumed and finally allowed to live.
